tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: List the signed-in Scout account's watches (store collection URLs being monitored), including cadence, active state, and last check time.

tools.name: add_watch
tools.description: Start watching a public store collection or category URL (e.g. a Shopify /collections/new-arrivals page) and email the account owner when new products appear. The first scan is a baseline: nothing is emailed. Watch out: the dogfood plan caps watches per account.

tools.name: update_watch
tools.description: Update one of the account's watches: rename it, change its check frequency, change when it emails you, add notes, or pause/resume scanning.

tools.name: delete_watch
tools.description: Remove a watch. The watch is archived (no further scans or emails); its stored items stay in Scout history.

tools.name: get_watch
tools.description: Inspect one watch in detail: its settings, the most recent scan result, and the newest products seen on the page.

tools.name: trigger_scan
tools.description: Run a scan of one watch right now. This on-demand scan does NOT email a digest; scheduled scans send the digest emails. Scans are locked for a few minutes, so repeat calls may report the in-flight scan instead.

tools.name: account_status
tools.description: Show the Scout account's plan, watch limit, allowed cadences, and how digest emails are delivered.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_watches, update_watch · Public sink: add_watch, trigger_scan · Destructive: delete_watch, trigger_scan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_watches, update_watch · Public sink: add_watch, trigger_scan · Destructive: delete_watch, trigger_scan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
